a94.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a94.name: Joe Biden
a94.title: US President
a94.speech: Said in a statement that "America and the world lost an extraordinary leader, statesman and humanitarian" as well as a man of "great character and courage, hope and optimism." Said, "With his compassion and moral clarity, he worked to eradicate disease, forge peace, advance civil rights and human rights, promote free and fair elections, house the homeless, and always advocate for the least among us. He saved, lifted, and changed the lives of people all across the globe." Declared January 9 a National Day of Mourning and called on "people of the world who share our grief to join us in this solemn observance."

a94.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a94.name: Donald Trump
a94.title: US President-elect
a94.speech: Urged everyone to keep the Carter family in their prayers, writing on Truth Social: "Those of us who have been fortunate to have served as President understand this is a very exclusive club, and only we can relate to the enormous responsibility of leading the Greatest Nation in History. The challenges Jimmy faced as President came at a pivotal time for our country and he did everything in his power to improve the lives of all Americans. For that, we all owe him a debt of gratitude."

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (on Rosalynn and his marriage)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (on Rosalynn and his marriage)
a94.speech: Said after Rosalynn's death that "as long as Rosalynn was in the world, I always knew somebody loved and supported me." After meeting Eleanor Rosalynn Smith in 1945, told his mother, "She's the girl I want to marry." Asked the secret of his enduring marriage, said: "Rosalynn has been the foundation for my entire enjoyment of life. First of all, it's best to choose the right woman, which I did. And secondly, we give each other space to do our own things. We try to be reconciled before we go to sleep at night and try to find everything we can think of that we like to do together. So we have a lot of good times." Said marrying Rosalynn was the "pinnacle" of his life.

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (1977 inaugural address on human rights)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (1977 inaugural address on human rights)
a94.speech: Vowed to put universal rights at the center of US foreign policy: "Our moral sense dictates a clear-cut preference for those societies which share with us an abiding respect for individual human rights. We do not seek to intimidate, but it is clear that a world which others can dominate with impunity would be inhospitable to decency and a threat to the well-being of all people."

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (1979 televised address on the energy crisis)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (1979 televised address on the energy crisis)
a94.speech: Said: "It is a crisis of confidence. It is a crisis that strikes at the very heart and soul and spirit of our national will. We can see this crisis in the growing doubt about the meaning of our own lives and in the loss of a unity of purpose for our nation."

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (memoir account of the Iran hostage crisis and 1980 election)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (memoir account of the Iran hostage crisis and 1980 election)
a94.speech: Wrote in his memoirs that his political future was out of his hands as the election approached: "Now, my political future might well be determined by irrational people on the other side of the world over whom I had no control. If the hostages were released, I was convinced my election would be assured; if the expectations of the American people were dashed again, there was little chance I could win."

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (2019, on Trump's reelection)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (2019, on Trump's reelection)
a94.speech: Warned Americans against reelecting Trump: "I think it will be a disaster to have four more years of Trump."

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (on his 1976 campaign persona)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (on his 1976 campaign persona)
a94.speech: Promised voters, "I'll never lie to you." Accepting his party's nomination at the 1976 Democratic convention, poked fun at his rise from obscurity, saying, "My name is Jimmy Carter and I'm running for president." In a Playboy interview, admitted he had looked on women with lust and "committed adultery in my heart many times."

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (1982 memoir 'Keeping Faith', on his post-presidency)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (1982 memoir 'Keeping Faith', on his post-presidency)
a94.speech: Wrote: "As one of the youngest of former presidents, I expected to have many useful years ahead of me."

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (reflections on his life and legacy)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (reflections on his life and legacy)
a94.speech: At an August 2015 news conference announcing his cancer diagnosis, said being president had been the highlight of his political career, and said he was at peace with his legacy: "I think I have been as blessed as any human being in the world." In his book 'A Full Life,' wrote that he was at peace with his accomplishments as president as well as his unrealised goals, and said he and Rosalynn were "blessed with good health and look to the future with eagerness and confidence, but are prepared for inevitable adversity when it comes."

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (2002 visit to Cuba)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (2002 visit to Cuba)
a94.speech: Called on the United States to end its "ineffective" economic embargo on Cuba, and challenged President Fidel Castro to hold free elections, grant more civil liberties and improve human rights.

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (2012 New York Times op-ed)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (2012 New York Times op-ed)
a94.speech: Accused the United States of "abandoning its role as the global champion of human rights," citing revelations that officials were targeting people, including US citizens, for assassination abroad as "disturbing proof" that the nation's stance on human rights had changed for the worse.

a94.speaker: Jimmy Carter, Former US President (2010, on the Carter Center's mission)
a94.name: Jimmy Carter
a94.title: Former US President (2010, on the Carter Center's mission)
a94.speech: Told an audience at the Carter Center in 2010: "We try to fill vacuums in the world by doing things that others don't want to do or cannot do because of diplomatic niceties. That's part of bringing peace."

a94.speaker: Jason Carter, Grandson of Jimmy Carter
a94.name: Jason Carter
a94.title: Grandson of Jimmy Carter
a94.speech: Told The Atlanta Journal-Constitution that the former president wanted to live long enough to cast a ballot for Democratic nominee Kamala Harris.

a94.speaker: Douglas Brinkley, Biographer of Jimmy Carter (on Carter's persona)
a94.name: Douglas Brinkley
a94.title: Biographer of Jimmy Carter (on Carter's persona)
a94.speech: Said, "He was never embarrassed to have a Georgian accent or be in blue jeans and play horseshoes and softball."

a94.speaker: Douglas Brinkley, Biographer of Jimmy Carter (on the hostage crisis and 1980 defeat)
a94.name: Douglas Brinkley
a94.title: Biographer of Jimmy Carter (on the hostage crisis and 1980 defeat)
a94.speech: Said, "It was a perfect storm of unpleasant events, and that inability of Carter to get those Iranian hostages released before the 1980 elections spelled doomsday."

a94.speaker: Andrew Young, US Ambassador to the United Nations under Carter
a94.name: Andrew Young
a94.title: US Ambassador to the United Nations under Carter
a94.speech: Said, "In the presidency, he got a sense of the fact that the world can be changed, and it doesn't take a government to change it; it can be changed one person at a time, one disease at a time, building one house at a time."

a94.speaker: Ronald Reagan, US President (1980 campaign)
a94.name: Ronald Reagan
a94.title: US President (1980 campaign)
a94.speech: Charged during the 1980 campaign: "A recession is when your neighbour loses his job. A depression is when you lose yours. And recovery is when Jimmy Carter loses his."

a94.speaker: The Carter Center
a94.name: The Carter Center
a94.speech: Said the 39th president, who had been in home hospice care since February 2023, died in Plains, Georgia, surrounded by his family.

a142.speaker: Mbabane consumer (anonymous)
a142.name: Mbabane consumer (anonymous)
a142.speech: Lamented: “The timing is terrible. The cost of everything is up and now they are raising bread prices again. Government should have found another way to support bakeries without punishing consumers.”

a142.speaker: Consumer from Simunye (anonymous)
a142.name: Consumer from Simunye (anonymous)
a142.speech: Highlighted the human cost: “Every lilangeni counts. When the price of bread goes up, it means skipping breakfast or sending a child to school on an empty stomach.”

a142.speaker: Eswatini Bakers’ Association
a142.name: Eswatini Bakers’ Association
a142.speech: Is citing escalating costs in yeast, sugar, packaging, labour and transportation that threaten bakery viability.

a142.speaker: Sibusiso Nxumalo, Chairperson of the Eswatini Bakers’ Association
a142.name: Sibusiso Nxumalo
a142.title: Chairperson of the Eswatini Bakers’ Association
a142.speech: Noted that the seven per cent was a compromise from a higher initial ask, aimed at balancing industry survival with consumer impact.

a142.speaker: Dr Thokozani Mamba, economist
a142.name: Dr Thokozani Mamba
a142.title: economist
a142.speech: Warned of broader implications: “Bread is one of the most visible price indicators. When bread goes up, it signals to the market that further increases are acceptable” ; calls for targeted subsidies to cushion low-income families, insisting that such hikes risk triggering rises in other commodities, further eroding purchasing power.

a142.speaker: Ministry of Labour and Social Security (second quarter report for the 2025 financial year)
a142.name: Ministry of Labour and Social Security (second quarter report for the 2025 financial year)
a142.speech: Reports that proactive labour inspections surged by 41 per cent to 587, thanks to new vehicles and inspectors, and that this enforcement has revealed a 63 per cent rise in redundancies when compared to the same period of 2024, leaving 2 056 employees jobless; the unregulated sector saw 171 redundancies.

a142.speaker: Ministry of Labour and Social Security
a142.name: Ministry of Labour and Social Security
a142.speech: Attributes this to a United States Presidential Order curtailing funding under the PEPFAR Project, hitting sectors like textiles and apparel, security and mining.

a142.speaker: Central Bank of Eswatini (data)
a142.name: Central Bank of Eswatini (data)
a142.speech: Recent Central Bank data shows that borrowing reached E8.8 billion by August 2025, up 2.8 per cent year-on-year.

a142.speaker: Trade unions
a142.name: Trade unions
a142.speech: Are pushing for a minimum wage of about E3 500.

a142.speaker: Economist (anonymous)
a142.name: Economist (anonymous)
a142.speech: Noted: “The greatest challenge preventing the ordinary liSwati from feeling richer is the high unemployment rate, compounded by ‘black tax’ obligations and the multi-billion projects often going to foreign companies, thus reducing local circulation of funds. Government has tried to argue that emaSwati do get a slice of the cake, but this is only an insignificant fraction of the amount leaving the country.”

a142.speaker: Lindiwe Vilakati, labour analyst
a142.name: Lindiwe Vilakati
a142.title: labour analyst
a142.speech: Observed: “Wages in the private sector have stagnated, yet the cost of living keeps climbing. Every new price increase widens inequality.”

a142.speaker: Nonophile Dlamini, resident
a142.name: Nonophile Dlamini
a142.title: resident
a142.speech: Complains: “This price hike feels like a cruel squeeze, making life measurably harder for the hardworking people of Eswatini.”

a338.speaker: Dr. Albert Opoku, Principal of Tepa Nurses and Midwifery Training College
a338.name: Dr. Albert Opoku
a338.title: Principal of Tepa Nurses and Midwifery Training College
a338.speech: Disclosed at the 2024 Matriculation Ceremony that all 785 fresh students are officially enrolled to pursue various programmes with the approval of the Ministry of Health and the Affiliate Institutions and have since pledged their allegiance to the authority of the college ; reminded the new students that their freedom at the College comes with some equivalent obligations and responsibilities in training students in academic and professional work ; charged them to be ambassadors of the College and stated that ambassadorial disposition in all interactions, wherever they find themselves, while adopting a very good attitude.

a338.speaker: Dr. Albert Opoku, Principal of Tepa Nurses and Midwifery Training College
a338.name: Dr. Albert Opoku
a338.title: Principal of Tepa Nurses and Midwifery Training College
a338.speech: Stated that the student population has increased from 82 in 2009 to 2,010 students and that the exponential increase in the student population is not corresponding to infrastructural development, especially classrooms, hostels, skills laboratory and ICT facilities ; indicated that infrastructural development, upon his assumption of office in August 2022, became his number one priority, giving birth to the construction of a 350 capacity hostel, 200 capacity classroom block and completion of the Ampem SRC Block ; announced that the construction of a dining hall facility started this year at the Anyinasuso campus, about 90 percent complete, after which a 1,500 capacity Assembly Hall will commence ; said all the projects are being funded from their Internally Generated Funds (IGF) with support from the Tepa Traditional Council, headed by the Tepamanhene, Nana Adusei Atwenewaa Ampem, and some individuals.

a338.speaker: Dr. Albert Opoku, Principal of Tepa Nurses and Midwifery Training College
a338.name: Dr. Albert Opoku
a338.title: Principal of Tepa Nurses and Midwifery Training College
a338.speech: Said the College has a strategic vision to offer the best in cutting edge research and service delivery in Nursing and Midwifery, as a result of which it has applied to Ghana Tertiary Education Commission to run a BSc Nursing programme, as envisaged by the Ministry of Health and the Government of Ghana; expressed the hope to complete all the processes to start the BSc Nursing by the next academic year ; hinted of collaboration between the College and Tikvah Africa, an international organisation, which offers knowledge and skill acquisitions and plans building a Solar Borehole and providing computers to support the College’s ICT Department ; revealed another collaboration with the University of Tsukuba of Japan for exchange programmes and local collaboration with the Municipal Hospital at Tepa ; said their partnership with the University of Cape Coast has allowed them to commence a process of introducing the Bachelor of Science in Nursing Programme on campus.

a338.speaker: Dr. Anthony Nsiah Asare, Presidential advisor on Health
a338.name: Dr. Anthony Nsiah Asare
a338.title: Presidential advisor on Health
a338.speech: Reminded the students that getting admitted into the health institutions was a privilege and tasked them to exhibit professionalism in their line of practice ; disclosed that the Health ministry was determined to ensure that there are health facilities across the country to help promote and prevent protracted ailments.

a338.speaker: Nana Bafour Appiah Frimpong, Twafohene of the Tepa Traditional Area, representing the Omanhene Nana Adusei Atwenewah Ampem I
a338.name: Nana Bafour Appiah Frimpong
a338.title: Twafohene of the Tepa Traditional Area, representing the Omanhene Nana Adusei Atwenewah Ampem I
a338.speech: Appealed to the government to provide additional facilities for the school; emphasised the need for critical amenities such as hostels and a school bus to enhance students’ academic experiences; highlighted the significant challenges students face due to the lack of adequate facilities and called on the government to prioritise their needs. “Providing these resources will greatly enhance the quality of education and reduce the burden on parents and teachers” ; reaffirmed the Tepa Traditional Council’s unwavering commitment to supporting educational development in the area and assured the school of their continued assistance.

a490.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a490.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a490.title: Djiboutian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a490.speech: Represented President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh at the 1218th meeting of the Peace and Security Council and, on his behalf, read out and conveyed a stirring message to the assembly concerning the ongoing conflict in Sudan.

a490.speaker: Chairperson of the African Union Commission (report)
a490.name: Chairperson of the African Union Commission (report)
a490.speech: Report on the situation in the Republic of Sudan, examined by the Council during the meeting.

a490.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a490.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.speech: In his message, expressed his gratitude to President Museveni for having convened this crucial meeting on Sudan, as well as to the Chairperson of the African Union Commission and the Executive Secretary of IGAD for their reports and their constant efforts to resolve the Sudanese crisis.

a490.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a490.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.speech: Stressed that Sudan has been plunged into a destructive war since April 2023, with fighting between the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) causing great suffering to the Sudanese people. Thousands of civilians have been killed and millions displaced. The humanitarian situation is disastrous, with numerous human rights violations reported.

a490.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a490.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.speech: Announced that Djibouti will host a meeting of all mediators in July, aimed at working on a coordinated approach focused on concrete results, notably the immediate cessation of hostilities.

a490.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a490.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.speech: Made several recommendations to the Council to promote a cessation of hostilities in Sudan, notably: 1. Call on the RSF and the SAF to immediately cease fighting in Darfur and other regions of Sudan. 2. Invite the RSF and the commander of the Supreme Council to meet under the auspices of the IGAD-African Union platform without delay. 3. Allow unconditional access to humanitarian aid for the Sudanese people. 4. Prepare the ground for an inclusive dialogue in Sudan in July. 5. Insist on accountability and launch investigations into the reported human rights violations.

a490.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a490.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti (message read to the Council)
a490.speech: Concluded by affirming that Sudan has reached a critical point where it risks breaking apart if the war continues unpredictably. The Peace and Security Council must not wait for this scenario to materialise, because the consequences could be disastrous.

a490.speaker: Djibouti, as Chair of IGAD
a490.name: Djibouti
a490.title: as Chair of IGAD
a490.speech: Has repeatedly called for a humanitarian ceasefire in the face of the crisis.

a572.speaker: European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO) report
a572.name: European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO) report
a572.speech: According to a report on Tuesday, restrictions are exacerbating an already dire humanitarian crisis affecting 77,000 people in Bugna and Lasta districts, North Wollo Zone of Ethiopia’s Amhara Region ; “telecommunications and banking systems are not working, and government structures have been absent for three months.” ; “The lack of humanitarian assistance and low crop production, coupled with high food prices, have exacerbated food insecurity.” ; 79 percent of pregnant and lactating women and 70 percent of children are acutely malnourished, with 9.2 percent severely so ; “Health challenges include 5,747 reported cases of malaria and increasing instances of scabies” ; 77 percent of residents lack access to clean water, while only 35% of primary school-aged children are regularly attending classes ; “In-kind food distributions by the World Food Programme and the Ethiopian Red Cross Society have begun,” and a Rapid Response Mechanism funded by ECHO has been activated to provide emergency nutrition, water, and sanitation support.

a572.speaker: Amhara regional government
a572.name: Amhara regional government
a572.speech: Blamed local militia for the blockade amid ongoing fighting between government forces and Amhara militants also known as Fano.

a572.speaker: Ambassador Shiferaw Teklemariam, Commissioner of the Disaster Risk Management Commission
a572.name: Ambassador Shiferaw Teklemariam
a572.title: Commissioner of the Disaster Risk Management Commission
a572.speech: Previously reported that security challenges in Bugna district have “hindered humanitarian aid access” but claimed the government has “sufficient resources and arrangements” to address the crisis.

a640.speaker: Daily Trust (newspaper)
a640.name: Daily Trust (newspaper)
a640.speech: reported under the headline, “Alleged sexual harassment: Senate dismisses Natasha’s petition against Apabio,” that the Senate declared Mrs Natasha’s sexual harassment and abuse of office petition against the Senate President dead on arrival. ; “Senate throws out Natasha’s ‘sensational’ allegation against Senate President Akpabio, says presentation violates rulebook.”

a640.speaker: Salient Times (newspaper)
a640.name: Salient Times (newspaper)
a640.speech: said, “Senate dismisses Natasha’s petition as invalid.”

a640.speaker: Blueprint (newspaper)
a640.name: Blueprint (newspaper)
a640.speech: reported, “Senate to Natasha: Sexual harassment petition against Akpabio dead on arrival.”

a640.speaker: Amebo (newspaper)
a640.name: Amebo (newspaper)
a640.speech: said, “‘Dead on arrival’ — Senate panel dismisses Natasha Akpoti’s petition against Akpabio.”

a640.speaker: Daily Sun (newspaper)
a640.name: Daily Sun (newspaper)
a640.speech: reported that, “Akpabio breaks silence on Akpoti.”

a640.speaker: Daily Independent (newspaper)
a640.name: Daily Independent (newspaper)
a640.speech: reported, ”At No Time Will I Ever Harass Any Woman, Akpabio Declares.”

a640.speaker: Tribune, Leadership, Punch and The Nation (newspaper cover pages)
a640.name: Tribune
a640.title: Leadership, Punch and The Nation (newspaper cover pages)

a640.speaker: The Matrix (newspaper)
a640.name: The Matrix (newspaper)
a640.speech: reported, “Budget Presentation Ultimatum Expires: Fubara, Assembly Set For Fresh Showdown.”

a640.speaker: News Direct (newspaper)
a640.name: News Direct (newspaper)
a640.speech: reported, “FG approves #10.3bn for diabetes kits, HIV drugs, after USAID suspension.”

a640.speaker: Business Day (newspaper)
a640.name: Business Day (newspaper)
a640.speech: According to Business Day, “Nigeria’s boldest budget faces execution hurdles.”

a928.speaker: Israel Katz, Israeli minister (press release)
a928.name: Israel Katz
a928.title: Israeli minister (press release)
a928.speech: “Humanitarian aid to Gaza? No electricity switch will be turned on, no water tap will be opened and no fuel truck will enter until the abducted Israelis return home.”

a928.speaker: Government of Israel
a928.name: Government of Israel
a928.speech: According to the Government of Israel, about 150 Israelis, foreigners and dual nationals were taken hostage by the Islamist movement Hamas.

a928.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a928.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a928.title: Israeli Prime Minister
a928.speech: Declared that the country is “at war” with Hamas.

a928.speaker: Palestinian Health Ministry
a928.name: Palestinian Health Ministry
a928.speech: Reported today that the death toll in the Gaza Strip has risen to 1,200 following an increase in Israeli bombardments, with a further 5,600 wounded counted.

a1072.speaker: Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC), 2024 national and sub-national HIV estimates and projections
a1072.name: Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC)
a1072.title: 2024 national and sub-national HIV estimates and projections
a1072.speech: Revealed that more than half of the people living with HIV/AIDS have not sought the life-saving antiretroviral therapy treatment; the commission reports that 334,721 people living with HIV, accounting for 47 per cent of that population, are currently on antiretroviral therapy treatment, with 52.6 per cent without treatment. The commission described the situation as "alarming", warning of its potential to derail national efforts to control the epidemic, and said the current situation had left the lives of the entire population, including non-HIV patients, at risk.

a1072.speaker: Isaiah Doe Kwao, Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation at the Ghana AIDS Commission
a1072.name: Isaiah Doe Kwao
a1072.title: Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation at the Ghana AIDS Commission
a1072.speech: Said the figures fell short of the global 95-95-95 targets set by UNAIDS, for 95 per cent of people living with HIV to know their status, 95 per cent of those diagnosed to be on treatment and 95 per cent of those on treatment to achieve viral suppression.

a1072.speaker: Isaiah Doe Kwao, Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation at the Ghana AIDS Commission
a1072.name: Isaiah Doe Kwao
a1072.title: Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation at the Ghana AIDS Commission
a1072.speech: Explained that 15,290 new HIV infections were recorded in 2024 alone, and that although 12,614 AIDS-related deaths were recorded, an estimated 12,358 deaths were prevented due to access to treatment; he said the data underscored the urgent need to expand access to antiretroviral therapy treatment. He stated that women and children continued to bear a disproportionate burden, with 68.5 per cent (10,303) of new infections occurring in females and 5.4 per cent (1,243) in children under 15; he remarked that although Ghana boasts that 99.3 per cent of HIV-positive mothers now receive prevention of mother-to-child transmission, more needed to be done to ensure effective follow-up and treatment, and added that the records for males were 4,987, while adults aged 15 and older recorded 11,289 out of the 15,290 new cases.

a1072.speaker: Nana Oye Bampoe Addo, Deputy Chief of Staff
a1072.name: Nana Oye Bampoe Addo
a1072.title: Deputy Chief of Staff
a1072.speech: Said issues such as misinformation, disinformation, stigma, discrimination, individual economic challenges, inadequate lifesaving services and recent funding cuts had contributed to derail progress. "Regardless, we are determined to ensure sustained domestic financing, including the recent suspension of USAID's international funding programme; integrate HIV priorities into broader health and development strategies, and adopt innovative, data-driven approaches to enhance service delivery. No one should be left behind in our HIV response," she emphasised.

a1072.speaker: Nana Oye Bampoe Addo, Deputy Chief of Staff
a1072.name: Nana Oye Bampoe Addo
a1072.title: Deputy Chief of Staff
a1072.speech: Cautioned that every HIV-positive person who was not on treatment was one step closer to advanced illness and AIDS-related death, which she said was unacceptable, and stressed that especially in present times there should not be such a wide treatment gap; as Ghana prepares to host the 2025 ICASA conference, she called on stakeholders, government institutions, health workers, donors, researchers, community advocates and civil society leaders to reflect deeply on the findings from these estimates and turn them into purposeful action.

a1298.speaker: Zebra Kasete, Vice President and Managing Director of Dundee Precious Metals Tsumeb
a1298.name: Zebra Kasete
a1298.title: Vice President and Managing Director of Dundee Precious Metals Tsumeb
a1298.speech: According to him, Tsumeb is the only place in the world where so many minerals can be found together. "More than 310 different minerals and gemstones have already been discovered here – and there will be more."

a1298.speaker: Clarissa Judmann, Cultural Attaché of the German Embassy
a1298.name: Clarissa Judmann
a1298.title: Cultural Attaché of the German Embassy
a1298.speech: Said at the opening that the project has a long history and that restoration work on one of the shafts already began in 2018. The German government has also already provided 15,000 euros (about N$30,000) for the development of the museum. "The aim was to restore the building so that it can be used as a museum. In addition, the existing samples and map archives must be preserved," she explained.

a1298.speaker: Zebra Kasete, Vice President and Managing Director of Dundee Precious Metals Tsumeb
a1298.name: Zebra Kasete
a1298.title: Vice President and Managing Director of Dundee Precious Metals Tsumeb
a1298.speech: Explained that he had recognised the significance of Tsumeb's rich mineral deposits on many occasions — the first time when he visited a mineral institute in Washington and discovered that an entire room there was reserved for samples of gemstones and minerals originating solely from Tsumeb. "When I meet older geologists, they often tell me that in the 1960s and 1970s it was every young geologist's dream to complete his studies in Tsumeb."

a1433.speaker: INTERPOL and the World Customs Organization (WCO) (operation announcement)
a1433.name: INTERPOL and the World Customs Organization (WCO) (operation announcement)
a1433.speech: Announced that nearly 20,000 live animals, all endangered or protected species, have been seized in a global operation against wildlife and forestry trafficking networks; that Operation Thunder 2024 (11 November - 6 December) brought together police, customs, border control, forestry and wildlife officials from 138 countries and regions, marking the widest participation since the first edition in 2017; that authorities arrested 365 suspects and identified six transnational criminal networks suspected of trafficking animals and plants protected by CITES; and that more than 100 companies involved in the trafficking of protected species were identified, with 2,213 seizures made worldwide.

a1433.speaker: Valdecy Urquiza, INTERPOL Secretary General
a1433.name: Valdecy Urquiza
a1433.title: INTERPOL Secretary General
a1433.speech: "Organized crime networks are profiting from the demand for rare plants and animals, exploiting nature to fuel human greed. This has far-reaching consequences: it drives biodiversity loss, destroys communities, contributes to climate change and even fuels conflict and instability. Environmental crimes are uniquely destructive, and INTERPOL, in cooperation with its partners, is committed to protecting our planet for future generations."

a1433.speaker: Ian Saunders, WCO Secretary General
a1433.name: Ian Saunders
a1433.title: WCO Secretary General
a1433.speech: "Operation Thunder continues to shed light on a crime that is often not a priority for enforcement actors. Through our joint efforts we have established cooperation mechanisms that facilitate the exchange of information and intelligence, and we have refined our enforcement strategies. The illegal wildlife trade is still rapidly growing, highly lucrative and has devastating effects. The WCO remains committed to supporting its members and partners to effectively combat this serious crime."

a1667.speaker: Embassy of the State of Eritrea, Washington, DC (official statement)
a1667.name: Embassy of the State of Eritrea
a1667.title: Washington, DC (official statement)
a1667.speech: Stated that the US Senate Foreign Relations Committee Hearing on East Africa, convened on 13 May, unfortunately repeats several misconceptions and unsubstantiated allegations against Eritrea, and that it is essential to clarify these matters based on verifiable facts. Said that as far as Eritrea is concerned, Senator Van Hollen's statements echo skewed media reports rather than established facts or nuanced analysis; that Eritrea is not mobilizing for war and has not been engaged in provocative military action or political brinkmanship against Ethiopia; that the specter of tension and apprehension in the region stems from unsettling Ethiopian pronouncements and frantic domestic media campaigns to acquire a "port and coastal territory through diplomatic and legal means if possible, and by force if necessary"; that this is an unacceptable proposition in international relations and fraught with unnecessary and avoidable destabilization of the region, and that the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and other relevant policy experts must call a spade a spade. It described Joshua Meservey's testimony as deplorable, provoking serious questions of underlying motive and intent, and underlined that such statements deliberately couched in ambiguous terms actually refer to and are euphemisms for the sovereign Eritrean territories – also endorsed in the EEBC Arbitral Ruling of 13 April 2002 – including Badme and other towns that remained occupied for almost two decades by previous Ethiopian regimes in flagrant violation of international law. Eritrean troops have otherwise fully redeployed, after the end of the war in Northern Ethiopia, and remain inside our sovereign territory.

a1667.speaker: Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland)
a1667.name: Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland)
a1667.speech: At the Hearing, raised concerns over a "boiling situation" between Eritrea and Ethiopia, singularly referring to Eritrea's alleged "military mobilization".

a1667.speaker: Joshua Meservey, former State Department official
a1667.name: Joshua Meservey
a1667.title: former State Department official
a1667.speech: Alleges, without ascertaining the true facts, that "Eritrean troops are still inside Ethiopian territory in Western Tigray".

a1699.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) report, shared with APA
a1699.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) report
a1699.title: shared with APA
a1699.speech: A report by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), shared with APA on Tuesday, paints a grim picture of the deteriorating situation for women and girls in Mali's conflict-affected regions; according to a survey in May 2025, the number of IDPs surged from 330,000 in May 2024 to about 380,000, a 15% increase, with growing reports of sexual exploitation, harassment, and forced marriages in displacement camps and conflict zones, particularly in Timbuktu, Gao, Mopti, and Ménaka; of the 6.4 million people in need of humanitarian assistance in Mali, over half are women and girls.

a1699.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a1699.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a1699.speech: "Women and girls are at the heart of these vulnerabilities and are disproportionately affected by the ongoing insecurity and humanitarian crisis," the UNFPA stated.

a1699.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a1699.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a1699.speech: The agency warns that without urgent additional funding, essential programmes to combat sexual violence and provide reproductive health services could collapse - putting nearly 900,000 women and girls targeted by these interventions at risk; of the $16.5 million needed for 2025, only $2.9 million has been secured, leaving a $13.5 million gap.

a1827.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva, International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director
a1827.name: Kristalina Georgieva
a1827.title: International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director
a1827.speech: Ahead of the IMF-World Bank Spring Meetings in Washington DC, cautioned small economies, including Malawi, to brace for trade shocks; said the global economic shifts triggered by rising tariffs, volatile markets and declining trust in multilateralism are a test of the resilience of fragile economies such as Malawi's.

a1827.speaker: Trade, Industry and Private Sector Development Partners
a1827.name: Trade
a1827.title: Industry and Private Sector Development Partners
a1827.speech: Urged Malawi to embrace effective policies to align private and public sector to achieve a viable socio-economic development; cited constraints in tourism such as inadequate supporting infrastructure and services as bottlenecks to success.

a1827.speaker: Akinwumi A. Adesina, African Development Bank (AfDB) president
a1827.name: Akinwumi A. Adesina
a1827.title: African Development Bank (AfDB) president
a1827.speech: Challenged African countries that in the wake of a rapidly changing global landscape, time has come for the continent to wean itself from aid dependency and chart its future through self-reliance, strategic partnerships and exploiting its vast natural resources.

a1827.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a1827.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a1827.title: Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a1827.speech: In the K8 trillion 2025/26 National Budget, projected grants at K1.14 trillion with K1.10 trillion coming from international organisations and K86.36 billion from foreign governments.

a1827.speaker: World Bank Group
a1827.name: World Bank Group
a1827.speech: Describes trade as a golden key towards ending global poverty because countries that are open to international trade tend to grow faster, become innovative, improve productivity and provide higher income as well as more opportunities.

a1966.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1966.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1966.title: President of South Africa
a1966.speech: Expressed his desire to meet his American counterpart, Donald Trump, in order to restore diplomatic relations between the two countries, damaged by the recent cuts in US aid and growing tensions; at a business conference in Johannesburg on Thursday he reiterated his wish to improve bilateral ties with the USA, particularly after Trump's executive order concerning land reform policies in South Africa; stressed the need to reach “a meaningful deal” with the United States in order to resolve several issues affecting relations between the two nations ; “We want to conclude a substantial agreement with the United States on a range of issues”.

a1966.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1966.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1966.title: President of South Africa
a1966.speech: Defended land reform in South Africa, insisting that it complies with the Constitution and seeks to repair the historical injustices linked to apartheid; rejected the accusations that current laws would allow arbitrary land seizures, specifying that expropriation would be carried out fairly.

a2153.speaker: Mandla Tshawuka, Minister of Agriculture of Eswatini
a2153.name: Mandla Tshawuka
a2153.title: Minister of Agriculture of Eswatini
a2153.speech: Strongly condemned the actions of those arrested, describing them as selfish and reckless, and said such behaviour undermines national efforts to contain the disease and protect the livestock industry: "This is witchcraft. These individuals are only looking out for their own interests while putting the entire nation's herd at risk. It is wrong and unacceptable."

a2153.speaker: Mandla Tshawuka, Minister of Agriculture of Eswatini
a2153.name: Mandla Tshawuka
a2153.title: Minister of Agriculture of Eswatini
a2153.speech: Urged farmers and business owners to take responsibility and comply fully with veterinary directives, warning that anyone found flouting the regulations would face the full force of the law: "Government has made it clear: these restrictions are not a suggestion, they are mandatory. Those who defy them put the livelihoods of thousands at risk." ; appealed for unity and cooperation, emphasising that the livestock industry's survival depends on collective action: "We cannot allow a few people's greed to undo the hard work being done to contain this disease." ; said they are dealing with a national crisis: "Anyone who disregards these measures is working against the country. Let us work together to defeat FMD and protect our farmers' livelihoods."

a2153.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture of Eswatini
a2153.name: Ministry of Agriculture of Eswatini
a2153.speech: Has imposed strict controls on the movement of cloven-hoofed animals, including cattle, goats and pigs, to curb the spread of the disease; according to the Ministry, Eswatini has previously experienced FMD outbreaks that led to significant losses; the Ministry has intensified surveillance, vaccination and awareness campaigns in affected areas.

a2153.speaker: Officials (Ministry of Agriculture, unnamed)
a2153.name: Officials (Ministry of Agriculture
a2153.title: unnamed)
a2153.speech: Noted that moving cattle without clearance not only risks spreading the disease to new areas but also threatens national and regional trade.

a2153.speaker: Authorities (Eswatini)
a2153.name: Authorities (Eswatini)
a2153.speech: Say investigations are on-going, and further arrests may follow if additional violations are discovered; authorities stress that cooperation from all stakeholders is the only way to protect the livestock sector and the broader economy.

a2153.speaker: World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH)
a2153.name: World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH)
a2153.speech: Recommends immediate reporting, strict movement controls, and vaccination as the primary tools for managing outbreaks.

a2178.speaker: Internal State Department document, cited by Africanews
a2178.name: Internal State Department document
a2178.title: cited by Africanews
a2178.speech: According to the document, the closure of embassies and consulates includes Lesotho, Eritrea, the Central African Republic, the Republic of Congo, the Gambia and South Sudan, as well as consulates in Durban (South Africa) and Douala (Cameroon), with responsibilities in these countries possibly transferred to neighbouring countries; the plan also includes closing embassies in European countries such as Malta and Luxembourg, as well as consulates in several cities in Europe and Asia.

a2178.speaker: Critics of the proposal
a2178.name: Critics of the proposal
a2178.speech: express concern that the reduction of the US diplomatic presence in Africa could diminish American influence on the continent, especially as other global powers, such as China, continue to expand their presence, and that the closures could also harm diplomatic relations, economic partnerships and the promotion of democratic values.

a2220.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Minister of Finance
a2220.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a2220.title: Minister of Finance
a2220.speech: Urged the members of the newly constituted Governing Board of the Ghana Revenue Authority to step up efforts to tackle tax evasion, smuggling, and corruption within the GRA, and called on the board to strengthen domestic revenue mobilisation as the government manages a difficult fiscal situation.

a2220.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Minister of Finance
a2220.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a2220.title: Minister of Finance
a2220.speech: Thanked President John Dramani Mahama for assembling what he described as a "distinguished team" to lead the GRA at what he called a crucial time for the economy ; "This is a defining moment. You assume this mantle at a time when the government faces tight financing conditions, with limited access to the capital market following the debt restructuring programme, and shrinking project and programme grants from development partners."

a2220.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Minister of Finance
a2220.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a2220.title: Minister of Finance
a2220.speech: Explained that the government's main fiscal goal for 2025 and the years ahead is to raise more domestic revenue, stating that the government aims to increase revenue collection by at least 0.6 percentage points of GDP each year, targeting a primary fiscal surplus of 1.5 percent of GDP by the end of 2025, and added that the country also seeks to reduce its external debt service-to-revenue ratio from 28 per cent in 2022 to 18 per cent by 2028.

a2220.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Minister of Finance
a2220.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a2220.title: Minister of Finance
a2220.speech: Pointed to the recent withdrawal of more than US$234 million in support from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) for health, education, and economic growth programmes, describing it as a reminder of the need to build a stronger domestic revenue base: "This is a stark reminder of why we must secure our own financing to support national development."

a2220.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Minister of Finance
a2220.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a2220.title: Minister of Finance
a2220.speech: Urged the new board and management of the GRA to modernise the Authority's operations, build a strong culture of integrity, and take firm action against tax evasion and smuggling, stressing that public trust in the GRA's fairness and ethical conduct was necessary for success and warning that "revenue lost through corruption translates to unbuilt schools, unpaved roads, and lives adversely affected by inadequate healthcare and poor sanitation."

a2220.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Minister of Finance
a2220.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a2220.title: Minister of Finance
a2220.speech: Announced a mandatory rotation policy for GRA officers every two years to minimise collusion and broaden staff experience, and mentioned plans to sign a performance bonus Memorandum of Understanding with the Commissioner-General, which would be witnessed by the heads of the Domestic Tax and Customs divisions.

a2220.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Minister of Finance
a2220.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a2220.title: Minister of Finance
a2220.speech: Assured the new board that the Ministry of Finance would support their efforts to carry out their responsibilities: "Let us remember that every tax cedi collected and every integrity-driven decision made brings us closer to building the prosperous, inclusive, and self-reliant Ghana We All Want Together."

a2421.speaker: United Nations / UNICEF Midline Evaluation of the Malawi Social Cash Transfer Programme (report)
a2421.name: United Nations / UNICEF Midline Evaluation of the Malawi Social Cash Transfer Programme (report)
a2421.speech: Says beneficiaries of the Social Cash Transfer Programme find cash transfers insufficient to meet all their needs while those who exit the safety net programme struggle to maintain their standard of living, and that the challenges impacting its effectiveness and sustainability are being compounded by discrimination and exclusion from other community programmes: "Beneficiaries often find the cash transfers insufficient to meet all their needs and those who exit the programme struggle to maintain their standard of living, facing difficulties in feeding their families, affording school fees and sustaining agricultural productivity."

a2421.speaker: UNICEF data
a2421.name: UNICEF data
a2421.speech: Show that at the end of 2024 the programme reached approximately 381,735 households and over 1.7 million individuals, including over 600,000 children; that recipient households have an average daily consumption of $0.32 per person per day prior to the programme; that even a tripling of this value would raise consumption to just under $1 a day per person, above the national poverty line but below the international poverty line of $3 per day; and that poverty and ultra-poverty headcount rates decreased by 11 and nine percentage points respectively among households who continuously received support relative to households whose support was discontinued.

a2421.speaker: Agness Nyirongo, economic governance officer at the Centre for Social Concern
a2421.name: Agness Nyirongo
a2421.title: economic governance officer at the Centre for Social Concern
a2421.speech: Said in a written response on Tuesday that while financial dependence is the programme's most visible vulnerability, the programme suffers from several design and operational shortcomings that reduce its effectiveness: "Without structural reform and stronger domestic commitment, these gains will remain temporary and fragile. Malawi now stands at a crossroads. We can either allow the programme to remain a donor-funded stopgap, or we can transform it into a nationally-owned, sustainably-financed and well-integrated pillar of our social protection system."

a2421.speaker: African Development Bank data
a2421.name: African Development Bank data
a2421.speech: Show that Malawi's actual disbursements have fallen short by 61.8 percent of the target in the 2024/25 financial year, following aid cuts and US tariff impositions.

a2421.speaker: Treasury (Malawi)
a2421.name: Treasury (Malawi)
a2421.speech: Projected grants at K1.17 trillion in the 2024/25 National Budget, of which K1.1 trillion was expected from international organisations and K72.69 billion from foreign governments.

a2421.speaker: Jean Sendeza, Minister of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare
a2421.name: Jean Sendeza
a2421.title: Minister of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare
a2421.speech: Was yet to respond to the newspaper's questionnaire.

a2421.speaker: Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare (strategic plan)
a2421.name: Ministry of Gender
a2421.title: Community Development and Social Welfare (strategic plan)
a2421.speech: The ministry, which coordinates implementation of the programme, hopes to increase coverage to 15 percent between 2022 and 2027 as outlined in the strategic plan; implementation of the five-year plan will require both increased overall funding and an increased proportional contribution from government.

a2586.speaker: Cecilia Lodonu-Senoo, Executive Director of Hope For Future Generations (HFFG)
a2586.name: Cecilia Lodonu-Senoo
a2586.title: Executive Director of Hope For Future Generations (HFFG)
a2586.speech: said Ghana can no longer rely solely on donor funding as global health financing dynamics shift, and called on the government to meet the country's co-financing obligations to secure the future of children; stressed the urgent need for local resource mobilization: "Vaccine sovereignty is very important; our children are key. Resources are no longer there. Everybody and all partners are calling for domestic resources, country ownership, and country-led initiatives. We cannot wait for our children to die from preventable diseases." ; She called for strong media advocacy to drive political will and transparency in the use of domestic funds for immunization.

a2586.speaker: Stephen Atasige, Country Coordinator of the Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI)
a2586.name: Stephen Atasige
a2586.title: Country Coordinator of the Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI)
a2586.speech: warned that delays in payment could have serious consequences: "The effects would be dire. Obviously, we're going to have shortages of vaccines, and consequently, we're going to have infectious diseases, especially among vulnerable children." ; He acknowledged the government's willingness to make payments but highlighted that current delays are problematic, indicating that vaccines are commodities that require urgent and timely acquisition, and recommended that Ghana consider making advance yearly payments for vaccines: "Vaccines are urgent life-savers and cannot be subjected to delays. Instead of waiting till then, we should pay. In fact, we are expected to pay for our vaccines within the first quarter because you need time for procurement procedures to complete."

a2586.speaker: Stephen Atasige, Country Coordinator of the Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI)
a2586.name: Stephen Atasige
a2586.title: Country Coordinator of the Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI)
a2586.speech: pointed out on accountability that the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Finance have systems in place, and UNICEF plays a role in vaccine delivery, but stressed the crucial role of the media in ensuring accountability by tracking vaccine availability: "When the government says it has paid for vaccines, the best form of accountability is that the vaccines are available and accessible at service delivery points."

a2586.speaker: Josephine Sackey, Executive Director of Socioserve Ghana
a2586.name: Josephine Sackey
a2586.title: Executive Director of Socioserve Ghana
a2586.speech: called on the government to explore sustainable funding mechanisms beyond foreign aid, suggesting avenues such as trust funds and dedicated taxes to bolster immunization and primary healthcare.

a2586.speaker: Joojo Cobbinah, Group Managing News Editor of EIB Network
a2586.name: Joojo Cobbinah
a2586.title: Group Managing News Editor of EIB Network
a2586.speech: encouraged journalists to humanize immunization stories, leading with compelling personal narratives backed by facts to better engage the public: "Stories should be about people. That is when people and society will remember the stories."

a2727.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a2727.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a2727.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a2727.speech: Highlighted Burundi’s efforts to contribute to the restoration of peace in the DRC and to improve diplomatic relations with Rwanda ; welcomed the European Union’s initiatives aimed at stabilising the region ; “I thank the European Union for having taken a responsible position in the face of this conflict,” referring to the recent sanctions imposed by Brussels on Kigali ; also stressed the importance of active involvement by the international community in order to stop the violence in the DRC before the situation becomes irreversible.

a2727.speaker: Ambassador Johan Borgstam, EU Special Representative for the Great Lakes region
a2727.name: Ambassador Johan Borgstam
a2727.title: EU Special Representative for the Great Lakes region
a2727.speech: Told the press: “We had a friendly, constructive and very instructive exchange with the President on the security and humanitarian situation in eastern DRC” ; announced that a visit would be organised on Wednesday 19 March 2025 in Cibitoke province to assess the living conditions of Congolese refugees and prepare humanitarian aid.

a3057.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
a3057.name: Mduduzi Matsebula
a3057.title: Minister of Health of Eswatini
a3057.speech: Emphasised the necessity of this move, positioning the restoration of the health sector as an imperative for achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and securing the nation's human capital for future prosperity.

a3057.speaker: Ministry of Health 2025/26 Second Quarter (July to September) Performance Report
a3057.name: Ministry of Health 2025/26 Second Quarter (July to September) Performance Report
a3057.speech: Details the specific cadres being prioritised for recruitment and deployment, including 104 nursing roles slated for immediate filling, the urgent recruitment of 115 Pharmacists and 37 Pharmacy Technicians to be completed by October 2025, and funding for 123 support staff positions.

a3057.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
a3057.name: Mduduzi Matsebula
a3057.title: Minister of Health of Eswatini
a3057.speech: "The current recruitment and deployment strategy is not an isolated measure; rather, it is anchored in the newly launched Human Resources for Health (HRH) Strategy 2025-2030. This long-term, comprehensive policy is designed to address the root causes of the health workforce crisis" ; "Continuous professional development and aligning local training institutions with national health needs are key to ensuring a sustainable supply of qualified health professionals for the future."

a3057.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
a3057.name: Mduduzi Matsebula
a3057.title: Minister of Health of Eswatini
a3057.speech: Confirmed that contractual terms strictly mandate suppliers to either replace or reimburse the cost of any recalled or substandard pharmaceuticals and medical supplies, and that should a supplier fail to honour this within 60 days, the Ministry can legally withhold equivalent funds from other outstanding payments to that supplier.

a3062.speaker: Shadiya Alimatou Assouman, Minister of Trade and Industry of Benin
a3062.name: Shadiya Alimatou Assouman
a3062.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Benin
a3062.speech: In her opening address, underlined the importance of this initiative for the Beninese economy: "This workshop is a crucial step for our nation. AGOA is a historic economic and commercial opportunity put in place by the American government which offers privileged access to international markets, particularly that of the United States, and it is an opportunity we must seize fully in order to strengthen our productive and competitive capacities" ; affirmed the government's willingness to support local companies in their export efforts in the face of the weakness of the supply of exportable products and the inability to meet the requirements of the American market ; "With the bold reforms undertaken to improve the business climate and the processing of raw materials, this trend will be reversed, with an increasingly marked and regular presence of high value-added, quality Beninese products on the American market."

a3062.speaker: Brian W. Shukan, Ambassador of the United States to Benin
a3062.name: Brian W. Shukan
a3062.title: Ambassador of the United States to Benin
a3062.speech: Encouraged Beninese companies to seize this opportunity: "For more than 20 years, AGOA has been the cornerstone of trade relations between the United States and Africa. This legislation allows thousands of African products to access the American market duty-free, thus offering African countries the possibility of fostering their economic growth and development" ; reaffirmed the commitment of the United States to supporting Beninese companies by facilitating access to one of the largest consumer markets.

a3091.speaker: Maria dos Santos Lucas, Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
a3091.name: Maria dos Santos Lucas
a3091.title: Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
a3091.speech: Explained that, in order to strengthen cooperation, the High Commissioner of Tanzania proceeded on Friday to present his credentials to the President of the Republic, Daniel Chapo, an act that reinforces cooperation between the two countries in various domains, with a focus on security and agriculture.

a3138.speaker: UNHCR (UN Refugee Agency)
a3138.name: UNHCR (UN Refugee Agency)
a3138.speech: Praises Burundi’s decision to grant refugees prima facie status, ensuring that they receive immediate protection and critical humanitarian assistance.

a3182.speaker: Karishma Pelham-Raad, Assistant Minister for International Organizations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia (speaking on behalf of President Joseph Nyuma Boakai)
a3182.name: Karishma Pelham-Raad
a3182.title: Assistant Minister for International Organizations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia (speaking on behalf of President Joseph Nyuma Boakai)
a3182.speech: Reaffirmed Liberia's steadfast commitment to humanitarian principles amid growing global crises; recognized the conference as "a beacon of hope and unity" and emphasized the essential principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, and voluntary service, stating, "In an increasingly turbulent world, where conflicts and disasters challenge our shared humanity, the work of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement has never been more crucial." ; "We are proud of the work being done in collaboration with the movement to provide lifesaving assistance, restore family links, and promote disaster preparedness. Through these actions, we demonstrate our shared commitment to alleviating human suffering and promoting a culture of peace and resilience."

a3182.speaker: Karishma Pelham-Raad, Assistant Minister for International Organizations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a3182.name: Karishma Pelham-Raad
a3182.title: Assistant Minister for International Organizations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a3182.speech: Highlighted several pressing global issues, including climate change, the refugee crisis, and the threats posed by pandemics: "These complex crises demand that we not only respond with immediate humanitarian assistance but also invest in long-term solutions that address the root causes of suffering and vulnerability," and emphasized that the global community must move beyond mere reactive measures and focus on building resilience in vulnerable populations.

a3182.speaker: Karishma Pelham-Raad, Assistant Minister for International Organizations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a3182.name: Karishma Pelham-Raad
a3182.title: Assistant Minister for International Organizations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a3182.speech: Called upon all member states and partners to deepen their cooperation and strengthen multilateral efforts in addressing humanitarian needs: "We must continue to ensure that humanitarian access is upheld in all circumstances," urging that the protection of civilians - especially women and children - should remain a priority in all collective efforts.

a3182.speaker: Karishma Pelham-Raad, Assistant Minister for International Organizations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a3182.name: Karishma Pelham-Raad
a3182.title: Assistant Minister for International Organizations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a3182.speech: In her closing remarks, expressed Liberia's heartfelt gratitude to the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement for its tireless dedication to humanitarian work: "We remain committed to supporting these efforts and working alongside all of you to advance our shared goal: a world where human dignity is protected, and every individual, regardless of circumstance, is given the support they need to thrive, flourish, and succeed."

a3345.speaker: Pete Hammond, Deadline awards columnist
a3345.name: Pete Hammond
a3345.title: Deadline awards columnist
a3345.speech: "Because it's got everything going for it in terms of acting, writing, directing" and many technical categories, "Shogun is probably going to be the top one," he told AFP.

a3345.speaker: Pete Hammond, Deadline awards columnist
a3345.name: Pete Hammond
a3345.title: Deadline awards columnist
a3345.speech: "I don't think the controversy is going to hurt it in terms of nominations," said Hammond of Baby Reindeer.

a3345.speaker: British woman who says she was the inspiration for the stalker in Baby Reindeer (lawsuit)
a3345.name: British woman who says she was the inspiration for the stalker in Baby Reindeer (lawsuit)
a3345.speech: Sparked a lawsuit saying she was the inspiration for the stalker and is demanding $170 million in damages.

a3465.speaker: Tom Alweendo, Minister of Mines and Energy (Namibia)
a3465.name: Tom Alweendo
a3465.title: Minister of Mines and Energy (Namibia)
a3465.speech: Emphasizes that the oil, gas, and green hydrogen industries in Namibia require skilled labour, technological advancements, and robust infrastructure.

a3465.speaker: Evelyn !Nawases-Taeyele, Deputy Minister of Urban and Rural Development
a3465.name: Evelyn !Nawases-Taeyele
a3465.title: Deputy Minister of Urban and Rural Development
a3465.speech: Has called on leaders at different levels to work in the best interest of and for the welfare of those they serve; she addressed the Annual General Meeting of the Namibia National Mayors' Forum, held at Swakopmund.

a3465.speaker: Independent Patriots for Change (IPC) (election manifesto)
a3465.name: Independent Patriots for Change (IPC) (election manifesto)
a3465.speech: Unveiled its election manifesto, with a budget of N$100 billion earmarked for national development if elected to power.

a3576.speaker: US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) (statement)
a3576.name: US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) (statement)
a3576.speech: Issued a statement at the 27 February event in Outapi on how support given through PEPFAR has been expanded from the earlier 14 constituencies in eight regions to 18 constituencies: “PEPFAR will continue this year to fund the OVC programmes with more than US$4 million, an amount that includes N$56 million in Namibian money, to ensure that OVC services continue in full and are expanded to 18 constituencies.”

a3582.speaker: Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a3582.name: Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a3582.speech: announced that the competition was officiated by 70 athletics judges meeting international refereeing standards.

a3582.speaker: Experts and coaches asked for comment by Reporter
a3582.name: Experts and coaches asked for comment by Reporter
a3582.speech: stated that the Federation is expected to arrange similar domestic competition opportunities at other distances as well, as it does with the Shambel Abebe Bikila Marathon.

a3582.speaker: Shambel Tolosa Kotu, former Ethiopian national team coach
a3582.name: Shambel Tolosa Kotu
a3582.title: former Ethiopian national team coach
a3582.speech: praised the preparation process that the Shambel Abebe Bikila Marathon is going through, but urged that, alongside the preparations, appropriate control and follow-up should be carried out so that competitions arranged in various countries through managers have the Federation's approval and are balanced against the athletes' overall needs and energy.

a3582.speaker: Shambel Tolosa Kotu, former Ethiopian national team coach
a3582.name: Shambel Tolosa Kotu
a3582.title: former Ethiopian national team coach
a3582.speech: citing the superiority Kenyan athletes took over Ethiopian athletes at the Eugene, Oregon Diamond League, said: "Kenyan athletes, like Ethiopians, have their own managers. But however much income the competitions arranged by their managers may bring them, they explain that their managers cannot make them compete on whatever schedule they wish unless it is in accordance with the timetable the athletes themselves set. The main reason for this is not only the strength of the athletes, but the fact that the national federation has a binding directive setting out what a manager's responsibilities and obligations are, and that athletes managed by a manager can do nothing without the Federation's recognition." ; said that at the Oregon Diamond League last Saturday Ethiopian women athletes were clearly outclassed by Kenyan athletes: "It is only because the Kenyans, unlike the Ethiopians, did not waste their energy on whatever competition came along, but kept themselves in reserve and carried out the preparation required for the competition in a studied manner."

a3582.speaker: Shambel Tolosa Kotu, former Ethiopian national team coach
a3582.name: Shambel Tolosa Kotu
a3582.title: former Ethiopian national team coach
a3582.speech: says that a Kenyan athlete who has competed once in a major international competition is expected to take sufficient rest and preparation before a second competition, whereas Ethiopian athletes, if it is said that something brings money, are seen competing without taking the rest and preparation the competition demands, looking only at the benefit they will obtain: "How long after one competition an athlete may take part in the next should be set down as a binding rule by the Federation"; he believes this would be of great help not only for the athlete's safety but also for the country and the people to sustain their interest in athletics, and underlined that it is necessary as a country for the national federation to prepare a competition directive approved by the manager, the athlete and the Federation.

a4024.speaker: United Nations Charter, Article 2 (document)
a4024.name: United Nations Charter
a4024.title: Article 2 (document)
a4024.speech: States in principle that nations are entitled to the exercise of their inalienable rights to self-determination and national independence, enabling states to decide freely on their own future to uphold the principles of national sovereignty and non-interference in the internal affairs of other states.

a4024.speaker: Paul Biya, President of Cameroon
a4024.name: Paul Biya
a4024.title: President of Cameroon
a4024.speech: Had declared that he could continue holding on to power until otherwise.

a4067.speaker: Eneas Emvula, Landless People's Movement (LPM) Member of Parliament
a4067.name: Eneas Emvula
a4067.title: Landless People's Movement (LPM) Member of Parliament
a4067.speech: Said there is a lack of opportunities for people over 35, who he said are often left out; he cited as an example the Green Hydrogen Scholarship, which supports Namibians between the ages of 18 and 35.

a4067.speaker: Dino Ballotti, Deputy Minister of Education, Innovation, Youth, Sports, Arts and Culture
a4067.name: Dino Ballotti
a4067.title: Deputy Minister of Education, Innovation, Youth, Sports, Arts and Culture
a4067.speech: Has acknowledged that his ministry received a petition on the 8th of July from unemployed graduate teachers, which highlights the challenges they face and includes their demands on how to address this problem.

a4067.speaker: Dr. Charles Mubita, Deputy Minister of Defence and Veterans Affairs
a4067.name: Dr. Charles Mubita
a4067.title: Deputy Minister of Defence and Veterans Affairs
a4067.speech: Says 12,702 veterans are still awaiting the N$170,000 payout promised under the Veterans Support Programme launched in 2011.

a4067.speaker: Members of Parliament in the National Assembly
a4067.name: Members of Parliament in the National Assembly
a4067.speech: Have raised concerns that women's empowerment initiatives are excluding rural women and neglecting the needs of boys in empowerment campaigns.

a4067.speaker: Ericah Shafudah, Minister of Finance
a4067.name: Ericah Shafudah
a4067.title: Minister of Finance
a4067.speech: Announced the implementation of the pension-backed housing scheme to improve access to decent and affordable housing mainly for civil servants who are not able to meet bank loan requirements.

a4067.speaker: Dino Ballotti, Deputy Minister of Education, Innovation, Youth, Sports, Arts and Culture
a4067.name: Dino Ballotti
a4067.title: Deputy Minister of Education, Innovation, Youth, Sports, Arts and Culture
a4067.speech: Has said the ministry is stepping up efforts to protect Namibia's indigenous languages.

a4067.speaker: Members of Parliament
a4067.name: Members of Parliament
a4067.speech: Have voiced their concerns regarding unaccredited institutions, discrimination in NSFAF funding, and unnecessary nursing evaluation tests.

a4067.speaker: Indileni Daniel, Minister of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
a4067.name: Indileni Daniel
a4067.title: Minister of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
a4067.speech: Says government is taking steps to better regulate gambling and sports betting in Namibia, acknowledging both the revenue potential and the risks associated with the growing industry.

a4067.speaker: Dr. Esperance Luvindao, Minister of Health and Social Services
a4067.name: Dr. Esperance Luvindao
a4067.title: Minister of Health and Social Services
a4067.speech: Says several local health programmes have been affected by the 90-day pause in United States foreign aid, including reduced support for healthcare workers and essential services.

a4088.speaker: Board of Directors of the African Development Bank Group
a4088.name: Board of Directors of the African Development Bank Group
a4088.speech: Approved a new $209 million Country Strategy Paper (CSP) for Lesotho, setting out a roadmap to accelerate the country's transition toward economic diversification, resilience, and inclusive growth over the next five years.

a4088.speaker: Moono Mupotola, African Development Bank Group Deputy Director General for Southern Africa and Country Manager for Lesotho
a4088.name: Moono Mupotola
a4088.title: African Development Bank Group Deputy Director General for Southern Africa and Country Manager for Lesotho
a4088.speech: "Lesotho stands at a critical juncture. This comprehensive strategy leverages the country's abundant water resources, strategic location, and demographic dividend to unlock new pathways for inclusive growth and economic diversification."

a4088.speaker: African Development Bank Group Country Strategy Paper (report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the AfDB)
a4088.name: African Development Bank Group Country Strategy Paper (report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the AfDB)
a4088.speech: According to the report, the new Country Strategy Paper builds on the lessons of past Bank operations in Lesotho and emphasizes integrated, multisectoral approaches, stronger implementation capacity, and proactive portfolio management. It aligns with Lesotho's National Strategic Development Plan II (2018-2028), the African Development Bank's Ten-Year Strategy (2024-2033), the African Union's Agenda 2063, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

a4214.speaker: Human Rights Watch (report of more than 100 pages)
a4214.name: Human Rights Watch (report of more than 100 pages)
a4214.speech: Accused Israel of committing crimes against humanity, of extermination and also acts of genocide, by intentionally depriving Palestinian civilians in the Gaza Strip of the basic goods necessary for survival; said the Israeli authorities intentionally prevented Palestinians in Gaza from accessing drinking water and basic sanitation since October 2023: “They restricted Gaza’s access to piped water, rendered most of Gaza’s water and sanitation infrastructure unusable by cutting off electricity and restricting fuel, deliberately destroyed and damaged water and sanitation infrastructure and water repair materials, and blocked the entry of essential water supplies” ; stated that for weeks the Israeli authorities cut off all water and prevented the entry of fuel, food and humanitarian aid into the Gaza Strip, which worsened the living conditions of the population.

a4214.speaker: Human Rights Watch (on Hamas)
a4214.name: Human Rights Watch (on Hamas)
a4214.speech: Says that Hamas, by perpetrating the attacks in southern Israel on 7 October 2023, also committed war crimes and crimes against humanity.

a4214.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Israel / Israeli government (statement)
a4214.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Israel / Israeli government (statement)
a4214.speech: Reacting to the accusation, accused the non-governmental organisation of lying in accusing Israelis of committing acts of genocide in the Gaza Strip by restricting access to water for civilians; in a statement, said the report is full of blatant lies and anti-Israel propaganda.

a4231.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti and acting chairman of IGAD
a4231.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a4231.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti and acting chairman of IGAD
a4231.speech: Set out the broad lines of a plan for a way out of the crisis for Sudan, beginning with the prior achievement of a ceasefire: “We believe that the continuation of the war threatens the unity and territorial integrity of Sudan and opens the way to foreign interventions aimed at dividing Sudan. That is why we call for a halt to the fighting.”

a4231.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti and acting chairman of IGAD
a4231.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a4231.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti and acting chairman of IGAD
a4231.speech: “The Republic of Djibouti considers the State of Sudan a brotherly country with which we maintain relations of kinship and fraternity. From this point of view, we are attached to the sovereignty of the State of Sudan, to the integrity of its territory, to its stability and to non-interference in its internal affairs.”

a4231.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti and acting chairman of IGAD
a4231.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a4231.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti and acting chairman of IGAD
a4231.speech: Welcomed that “regional and international initiatives have been launched since the beginning of the fighting on 15 April to end the conflict and find peaceful solutions to the crisis” ; recalled that “within IGAD, we rapidly presented an initiative aimed at stopping the war from the very first moment, because Sudan is an established and active member of our organisation” ; paid tribute to the “important role played by the brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, represented by the Jeddah platform, alongside the United States of America, the African Union and IGAD, in opening the way to dialogue among Sudanese” ; “Today, we observe that all the initiatives are going in the same direction”, calling “for the coordination of regional and international initiatives” and indicating that “the initiative of IGAD, the African Union and the Jeddah Platform is the most appropriate for finding a solution to the problem”

a4231.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti and acting chairman of IGAD
a4231.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a4231.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti and acting chairman of IGAD
a4231.speech: Linked the definitive settlement of the Sudanese crisis to the capacity “of the vital forces of this brotherly country to commit to implementing the results of the dialogue and to working for national reconciliation”, and closed his intervention by reiterating “Djibouti’s readiness to provide all assistance to Sudan, whether at the level of bilateral relations or through its current chairmanship of IGAD” ; hoped that “this brotherly country will return to peace, stability and national concord” and that “its generous people will benefit from its riches”

a4231.speaker: Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan, president of the Transitional Sovereign Council of the Republic of Sudan
a4231.name: Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan
a4231.title: president of the Transitional Sovereign Council of the Republic of Sudan
a4231.speech: Gave an account of the situation currently prevailing in Sudan and reported his government’s determination to work for the return of peace, stability and national concord in his country.

a4252.speaker: National Police of Cabo Verde (police source)
a4252.name: National Police of Cabo Verde (police source)
