a6558.title: outgoing EU Ambassador to Malawi (Daily Nation interview)
a6558.speech: "The fight against corruption has not improved… despite international support." ; "There was nobody in the country leading by example to fight corruption." ; By linking the disappearance of public funds in the health and education sectors to elite impunity, Skinnebach makes it clear that Malawi is no longer merely facing a corruption problem.

a6558.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, outgoing EU Ambassador to Malawi (Daily Nation interview)
a6558.name: Rune Skinnebach
a6558.title: outgoing EU Ambassador to Malawi (Daily Nation interview)
a6558.speech: Reflected on "the envy which was corruption Bureau" — a reference to the Anti-Corruption Bureau, once respected in the region, having become a shadow of its former self.

a6558.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, outgoing EU Ambassador to Malawi (Daily Nation interview)
a6558.name: Rune Skinnebach
a6558.title: outgoing EU Ambassador to Malawi (Daily Nation interview)
a6558.speech: On Malawi's deteriorating public services: "Hospitals are very rudimentary… schools not up to level… public money disappearing."

a6558.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, outgoing EU Ambassador to Malawi (Daily Nation interview)
a6558.name: Rune Skinnebach
a6558.title: outgoing EU Ambassador to Malawi (Daily Nation interview)
a6558.speech: "Development partners can only support existing [anti-corruption] initiatives." ; "The ball is in Malawians' hands."

a6558.speaker: Daily Nation, "EU Envoy: Malawi Corruption Fight Failing" (Exclusive Interview, July 11, 2025)
a6558.name: Daily Nation
a6558.title: "EU Envoy: Malawi Corruption Fight Failing" (Exclusive Interview, July 11, 2025)
a6558.speech: Cited as the source of the outgoing EU Ambassador's farewell interview remarks on Malawi's failing anti-corruption fight.

a6709.speaker: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report, presented in Nampula
a6709.name: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.title: presented in Nampula
a6709.speech: Released indicators showing that the national average rate of chronic malnutrition stands at 37 percent, while in Nampula the figures point to 46.7 percent, Cabo Delgado 44.7 and Zambezia 42.7; the data were collected between 27 July 2022 and 27 February 2023.

a6709.speaker: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.name: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.speech: Reveal that Mozambique has recorded improvements in the health conditions of the population over the last 25 years; concluded that Mozambique's population is young, since 48 percent are under 15 years old, and that 32 percent of households are headed by women, with an average of 4.6 members.

a6709.speaker: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.name: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.speech: Data gathered indicate that, in Mozambique, 31 percent of children under five years of age are registered with the authorities, the best performance being the city of Maputo with 62 percent and Nampula province the worst with 25 percent.

a6709.speaker: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.name: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.speech: Writes that, in Mozambique, at least 52 percent of the population has access to sources of drinking water, the best figure being in the city of Maputo with 99 percent and the worst indicators in Zambezia with 37 percent and Nampula with 38 percent.

a6709.speaker: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.name: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.speech: Reports on women's health that 48 percent adopted modern family planning methods, with Zambezia province trailing at 25 percent and Maputo province best at 82 percent; as regards childbirth, 68 percent of women in the country had the assistance of professionals in maternity wards.

a6709.speaker: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.name: Fourth Demographic and Health Survey (IDS 2022-23) final report
a6709.speech: Found that, in the country, malaria had a prevalence of 32 percent, with the best figure recorded in the city of Maputo, less than one percent, and the worst in Nampula province, at 55 percent.

a6800.speaker: Vincent Nmehielle, African Development Bank Group Secretary General
a6800.name: Vincent Nmehielle
a6800.title: African Development Bank Group Secretary General
a6800.speech: Said the dismantling of USAID aid should make African countries, including Uganda, rethink their development financing; says the continent should not continue bemoaning the fact that President Donald Trump withdrew USAID funding but rather say it is time to move on, time to focus and time use resources better ; “After that decision is made, how do you respond? Do you keep crying saying that the US has removed the money so we are no longer able to develop? That means you will not exist if that fund doesn't exist.” ; “I would like to think that Africa has the resources it needs in order to drive its own development. One lesson that I have learnt in development economics is that development is a ‘do it yourself'.”

a6800.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6800.name: Marco Rubio
a6800.title: US Secretary of State
a6800.speech: Announced on March 10 that he had cut 83% of U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) programs, which provides humanitarian and development assistance worldwide.

a6800.speaker: Development experts and charities
a6800.name: Development experts and charities
a6800.speech: Have indicated that the cuts will severely affect development programing in African countries.

a6800.speaker: Kevin Urama, Chief Economist and Vice-President for Economic Governance and Knowledge Management at African Development Bank Group
a6800.name: Kevin Urama
a6800.title: Chief Economist and Vice-President for Economic Governance and Knowledge Management at African Development Bank Group
a6800.speech: Told journalists that Trump's tariffs are a wakeup call to Africa: “It is all about trade. Isn't it? Trading what you produce with others. The relevance of African Free Continental Area is here. Can you imagine this continent trading within its self?” ; “You need to interrogate whether or not the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is a reality. More so now. But the AFDB will support every country that has found an avenue. We can work with them to fine tune how to proceed.”

a6800.speaker: Vincent Nmehielle, African Development Bank Group Secretary General
a6800.name: Vincent Nmehielle
a6800.title: African Development Bank Group Secretary General
a6800.speech: Suggests that African leaders have to look inward and use the continent's capital to work for it; said the continent can boost productivity and thereby reduce borrowing if it improves domestic revenue mobilization and works on investing fiscal resources, her savings, her sovereign wealth funds and pension funds ; “If Africa is able to do governance better in order to improve transparency, close illicit financial flows, things will change. Africa loses almost ninety billion dollars every year. That is far much more than we get from aid and Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) every year.”

a6800.speaker: United Nations report (2024)
a6800.name: United Nations report (2024)
a6800.speech: Found that Africa's external debt had climbed to more than $650 billion, and debt servicing costs reached nearly $90 billion; observed that over 40 per cent of African countries allocated more funds to debt service than to health — a stark reflection of how debt obligations are undermining Africa's development goals.

a6800.speaker: UNDP report (launched April 2023)
a6800.name: UNDP report (launched April 2023)
a6800.speech: Estimated the impact of biased credit ratings on African countries at $74.5 billion.

a6800.speaker: Economists
a6800.name: Economists
a6800.speech: Say that while sovereign bonds provide a stable financing avenue devoid of preconditions akin to multilateral concessional funding, their repayment terms are contingent upon global credit ratings.

a7242.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.speech: Said on Tuesday that escalating conflict and a deteriorating food security situation have forced over 300,000 people to flee their homes in northern Mozambique ; the report said the population displaced from Cabo Delgado province was forced to abandon their crops and has been left completely reliant on humanitarian assistance ; added that displacement of communities has been seen in Cabo Delgado for years, with the province "experiencing attacks by non-state armed groups" since 2017.

a7242.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.speech: Said the latest violence had forced thousands of refugees across the border into neighboring Tanzania and raised "concerns over the regionalization of the conflict."

a7242.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.speech: Said it "urgently needs $4.7 million per month to assist those internally displaced in northern Mozambique" ; warned that "Without additional funding WFP will be forced to reduce food rations as early as December."

a7242.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.speech: Said: "The situation is even more worrisome given that Cabo Delgado has the second highest rate of chronic malnutrition in the country, with more than half of children under the age of five chronically malnourished."

a7242.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a7242.speech: Said that "despite significant operational challenges," it was collaborating with the Mozambique government "to reach 310,000 people each month in the provinces of Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa with food, vouchers and nutrition support."

a7242.speaker: Antonella D'Aprile, WFP Representative for Mozambique
a7242.name: Antonella D'Aprile
a7242.title: WFP Representative for Mozambique
a7242.speech: "We are deeply concerned about the unfolding humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado where conflict and violence have left people without access to food and livelihoods." ; "The growing insecurity and poor infrastructure have meant that reaching out to people in need has become harder and now with COVID-19, the crisis becomes even more complex."

a7242.speaker: FEWSNET (famine early warning system)
a7242.name: FEWSNET (famine early warning system)
a7242.speech: Latest findings indicate that communities will continue to face 'crisis' levels of food insecurity (IPC Phase 3) into early 2021.

a7242.speaker: Lola Castro, WFP (@LolaCastroWFP, Twitter post)
a7242.name: Lola Castro
a7242.title: WFP (@LolaCastroWFP, Twitter post)
a7242.speech: "@WFP is extremely concerned about the deteriorating food security situation in #CaboDelgado, #Mozambique, where over 300,000 people have fled their homes & villages, abandoning their crops due to insecurity. Learn more"

a7266.speaker: Mozambican Health Ministry
a7266.name: Mozambican Health Ministry
a7266.speech: Announced on Wednesday that it distributed across the country, over the last five months, medicines and other medical products budgeted at 9.4 billion meticais (147.1 million US dollars, at the current exchange rate).

a7266.speaker: Ussene Isse, Mozambican Health Minister
a7266.name: Ussene Isse
a7266.title: Mozambican Health Minister
a7266.speech: Answering questions on the availability of medicines from deputies in the Assembly of the Republic, said the medicines distributed are for the treatment of the most frequent diseases in the country and which cause the greatest concern for public health “namely diarrhoea, respiratory diseases, high blood pressure, diabetes, tuberculosis, malaria, and HIV/AIDS. The medicines are distributed on a quarterly basis” ; revealed that there are currently sufficient stocks of essential medicines for the next six months, “however, the sector is facing some restrictions in relation to medicines for the cardiovascular and nervous systems” ; “The missing items will be restocked in June and July”, he promised. “It is important to stress that for these items there are alternative formulations of the same medicine or other therapeutic options with the same medicinal functions”.

a7266.speaker: Ussene Isse, Mozambican Health Minister
a7266.name: Ussene Isse
a7266.title: Mozambican Health Minister
a7266.speech: Said the Health Ministry will continue to track medicines through electronic systems “in order to stop the constant reports of theft of drugs and other medical equipment” ; “It means that the medicines that are going to enter Mozambique from now on will have a seal and this seal, when violated, is connected to an electronic system. It means that digitalization is going to bring revolution to the sector and will help us to control and know where the medicine is being sold or marketed” ; said that as a result of the theft of medicines, five health professionals have already been expelled from the National Health System, though he did not mention the units or regions in which they were operating.

a7266.speaker: Ussene Isse, Mozambican Health Minister
a7266.name: Ussene Isse
a7266.title: Mozambican Health Minister
a7266.speech: Announced the acquisition and installation of a total of 100 ultrasound scanners and 29 fixed X-ray machines in various health facilities across the country. “We are going to finish building seven new health units, namely the Mocímboa da Praia, Mueda, Meconta, and Mopeia district hospitals, in the northern province of Cabo Delgado; and the Nampula, Mavalane and José Macamo General Hospitals”, he said; also said the government intends to hire, during the current year, 724 new health professionals.
